title.orig: Endymion, Book I, lines 1–33: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever
title.en: Endymion, Book I, lines 1–33: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever
title.zh: 恩底弥翁（第一卷开头三十三行）：美的事物是永恒的喜悦

edition.en: First edition, London, 1818, as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 24280)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 24280 所录 1818 年伦敦初版

basis.en: Published in 1818; the author died in 1821.
basis.zh: 1818 年出版；作者卒于 1821 年。

note.en: The opening thirty-three lines of Keats’s long romance, written when he was twenty-two. Reviewers mocked the poem as a whole; its first line became proverbial. Notice that beauty here is not decoration but shelter, a bower that keeps us, and that “all lovely tales that we have heard or read” are counted among the things of nature.
note.zh: 济慈长篇传奇诗的开头三十三行，写成时他二十二岁。评论家嘲讽了整首诗；它的第一行却成了格言。留意这里的美不是装饰，而是庇护——一座护着我们的凉亭；也留意“我们听过或读过的一切可爱的故事”被算进了自然之物里。

excerpt.zh:
美的事物是永恒的喜悦：
它的可爱与日俱增；它永远不会
消逝成虚无；

note.en: The first line became a proverb and the passage is lush and generous, but it is the opening of a long poem Keats himself called immature, and it shows.
note.zh: 首句成了格言，文字丰美，但这是济慈自认“不成熟”的长诗开头，痕迹看得出来。
